summary.text: Steve Stadelman is a member of the Illinois Senate for the Rockford-based 34th District, first elected in 2012.
His official biography says he worked for 25 years as a television news anchor and reporter at WTVO-Channel 17 before entering public office.

paragraphs.text: Stadelman grew up on a small dairy farm in southern Wisconsin, attended Brodhead High School, and holds a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
His biography says he worked as a television news anchor and reporter for 25 years before running for the Senate.
Citizens in the 34th District elected Stadelman with 64 percent of the vote in 2012, according to the biography.

It says that in 2019 he co-sponsored legislation allowing a casino in Rockford and secured $275 million toward passenger rail between Chicago and Rockford, and that he was named Legislator of the Year in 2018 for his work on the Rivers Edge tax credit.
